Definition: adverb from G3717; in a straight manner, i.e. (figuratively) correctly (also morally):--plain, right(-ly).
BiblicalUsage: Rightly can mean correctly judged or plainly spoken. Jesus told the lawyer, Thou hast rightly judged, and when He healed the man who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech, the man spake plain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe judging rightly is a skill worth learning: the lawyer answered rightly, and the deaf man's tongue was loosed to speak plain.
